# Where to Watch The Wingfeather Saga Read & Watch


by Angel | October 1, 2026


What changes when a beloved book becomes an animated series—and what stays exactly the same?


For fans of Andrew Peterson’s *The Wingfeather Saga* , *The Wingfeather Saga Read & Watch* offers a chance to go behind the scenes and explore how the beloved fantasy series made the journey from page to screen. Executive Producer J. Chris Wall and special guests discuss the creative choices, additions, changes, and similarities that shaped the animated adaptation.


[Watch The Wingfeather Saga Read & Watch now on Angel.](https://www.angel.com/watch/wingfeather-saga-read-and-watch)


### **From the Page to the Screen**


Adapting a beloved book series is about more than simply recreating what’s already on the page.


Books and animated series tell stories in different ways. A novel can spend pages inside a character’s thoughts or describe a world in intricate detail. Animation can communicate through movement, music, voice acting, visual storytelling, and the performances of its characters.


*The Wingfeather Saga Read & Watch* explores what happens when those different forms of storytelling meet.


Through conversations with the people involved in the series, viewers can discover why certain elements changed during the adaptation process, why others remained, and how creative decisions helped bring Andrew Peterson’s world to life on screen.


### **A Conversation for Fans of the Books and the Show**


You don’t have to choose between being a book fan and a fan of the animated series.


*The Wingfeather Saga Read & Watch* gives both audiences something to explore. Readers can see how familiar moments and characters were translated to animation, while viewers who discovered Aerwiar through the show can learn more about the books that started it all.


The conversations also make room for younger fans. One Angel Guild member appreciated having a child included in the discussion, while another praised the series for creating a thoughtful, cross-generational conversation about books.


That makes *Read & Watch* more than a behind-the-scenes feature. It can be a way for families to talk together about the stories they love—and perhaps encourage kids to pick up the books for the first time.


### **A Companion for the Whole Family**


Some behind-the-scenes features are made for adults who want to know how something was produced. *The Wingfeather Saga Read & Watch* takes a broader approach.


The conversations are designed to be accessible to fans of different ages and different levels of familiarity with the books and show. Kids can learn more about the creative process behind a series they enjoy, while parents can discover new ways to talk about reading and storytelling with their children.


One Guild member called it “a great example of how to have a polite, inclusive, thoughtful conversation about a book” and a reminder for parents to take the time to read what their children are reading.


That may be one of the best reasons to watch together: it turns a shared love of a story into a shared conversation about how stories are made.


### **Watch** ***The Wingfeather Saga Read & Watch*** **on Angel**


Whether your journey to Aerwiar began with Andrew Peterson’s books or the animated series, *The Wingfeather Saga Read & Watch* offers a deeper look at both.


Join Executive Producer J. Chris Wall and special guests as they explore the changes, similarities, and creative choices behind the journey from page to screen.
